subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a Warcraft-style swamp troll design—hunched posture, long arms, tusks, mohawk, bone fetishes, loincloth, swamp base—aiming for a rich but manageable module using joint, chain, sweep, part, capsule, spike, and extrude constructs.

I'm sketching the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, a spine chain curving forward for the hunch, then a neck chain branching to a head joint, with careful parenting so each segment connects properly to the previous tip joint. I'm also planning a jaw joint positioned relative to the head using direct model coordinates to keep things simple and avoid tricky API edge cases.

Now I'm defining the torso as a sweep along the spine chain, varying the radius from narrower hips to a wider chest, and starting to think through the skin paint/material setup.

For skin, I'm going with a swamp-troll palette, teal-green mottled skin with countershading to add depth. Then I'm setting up the legs as limb chains from hip to foot, calculating segment lengths and forward knee bends so the proportions stay anatomically reasonable.

Still planning rig geometry... adding feet with clawed toe spikes and sketching out long-armed proportions with knuckles near the ground, working out shoulder-to-hand distances and elbow bend directions.

For hands, I'm deciding to make big fist boxes with three finger spikes as claws, and considering whether to build fingers as simple single joints parented to the wrist rather than full chains to keep things cheap.

Toes can just be rigid foot props without separate joints, keeping things moderate. For the head, I'm planning a skull sphere with heavy brow and big jaw, scaling the upper head and muzzle, then setting up a jaw joint and hinge bone to drive the lower jaw frustum shape.

Now I'm sweeping curved tusk shapes upward from the lower jaw using bezier control points, mirrored left and right in ivory with pointed caps, positioned to curve up beside the nose like classic troll tusks. I'm placing the neck end and head center coordinates to set up the overall troll head proportions with its characteristic long nose.

Head and brow continuation: I'm defining the skull sphere dimensions, adding an angled brow box, and figuring out how to apply glowing eye textures as decals on the skull surface, working out the right placement coordinates so the eye planes sit correctly on the curved skull surface without clipping inside or floating outside it.

Now I'm sketching the nose as a hooked bezier sweep from the brow down to a tip with small dark nostril spheres, then building the muzzle and jaw as tapered frustum boxes with bone-colored heads, and adding a dark interior box for the mouth cavity.

Next I'm shaping the ears as extruded pointed outlines swept upward and back, working out the direction vector and outline points carefully so the shape stays sharp without self-intersecting.

Still writing ear geometry...

Still writing blade extrusion logic...

Mapping blade positions along the spine curve, I'm tracing the body's surface geometry from head to upper back to figure out where each blade should sit against the neck and spine radii.

Rather than hand-tuning coordinates, I decide to cast downward rays onto the body and skull surfaces to find exact landing points for each mohawk blade, letting the hit results inherit the correct bone for rigging.

I need to shift the hit point down slightly and explicitly assign the bone from the raycast result, falling back to head if null. Now I'm thinking about shoulder armor — a combination of skin, leather pauldron domes, and bone spikes, kept roughly symmetric on both sides rather than going fully asymmetrical.

For fetishes, I'm planning a bone necklace at the neck base using a draped closed curve around the collar area with rough points, accepting that the drape-to-surface approach might give slightly odd results but should work well enough.

For fetishes, I'm skipping a held staff since the hand pose is extended fingers, and instead planning hanging bone totems off the belt—skull, feather, bone cross—plus shoulder spikes, tusk wraps, and bone arm bands. I'll also add base props like a gnarled stump and a small totem pole with a glowing green skull.

I'm designing the base as a circular mud/water disc with lily pads, mushrooms, reeds, and a bubbling green glow, and working out the exact vertical placement so the troll's feet sit just above the disc's top surface while the lowest point of the whole model still grazes floor level.

I'm also planning the texture set — eye, war paint stripes, loincloth tribal pattern, pendant rune, totem face, lily pad and reed cards, tusk wrap — aiming for around seven distinct textures, and sketching out the loincloth's front and back flaps.

Writing extrude shape code...

Still shaping body proportions... I'm defining a radius function for the torso that tapers with a slight pot-belly bulge, then widening the chest and shoulders where the arm joints attach, with the hip pelvis getting its own extra sphere for bulk.

Now I'm working through the arms, tapering the radius from shoulder to wrist with a slight forearm swell for that long-troll-arm look, then building the hand as a small fist box at the wrist with spiked claw-like fingers and a thumb positioned slightly forward and spread in a relaxed resting pose.

For the feet, I'm placing the ankle target near ground level, attaching a foot box offset forward and down from it, and adding three claw-like toe spikes at the front, while working out the leg chain's hip-to-foot distances to set proper segment lengths.

For the arms, I'm placing the shoulders on the chest below the spine tip, aiming hand targets outward and down to get a good distance for two-segment arm lengths, and setting pole hints so elbows bend outward and back naturally.

For the neck, I'm building a two-joint chain from the base of the spine up to just below the head, with the head itself parented to the top neck joint and aimed slightly upward and forward, tapering the radii so the neck narrows toward the head.

Now I'm defining the jaw joint parented to the head, aimed downward and forward to form the mouth opening, then assigning role labels across the skeleton (spine, neck, leg, arm, finger) so each chain type is identifiable. For the head geometry, I'm starting to build the skull as a scaled, flattened sphere positioned above the neck, attached to the head bone with its own transform and scale options.

Adding brow ridge and eye decals...

Adding undershot lower jaw geometry...

Positioning the tusk control and tip points outside the muzzle width, then considering adding small gold bands as tori oriented along the tusk's tangent direction using frame-based placement at a point partway up the tusk.

I'm sketching the nose as a bezier sweep with a hooked tip and tapering radius, plus small dark sphere nostrils near the tip. I'll skip cheek spikes but note face paint stripes as a possible decal detail.

Now I'm placing cheek war-paint decals angled outward from the skull, considering a sparse chin tuft or dreadlock-style hair for the troll's mohawk look, and adding ear rings. For skin, I'm building a custom paint function layering mottled base texture with moss patches appearing on upward-facing surfaces based on noise thresholds.

I'm settling on a teal-green skin palette with darker shadow tones and a sage belly countershade, plus defining leather, bone, and gold material colors for the gear.

Now I'm sketching the pauldron shoulder pads using lathed dome shapes with an outlined profile tilted outward at the shoulder joint, then planning to add bone spikes onto the pad for extra detail.

Still writing spike code...

Next I'm thinking about adding arm bands as torus-like rings swept around the upper arm.

I'll make the belt a loop around the hips, then build a leather sweep along that loop with beads attached. For hanging fetishes I'll grab points along the loop and drop cords down from each, using bone positions for the hip joint.

Now figuring out loop orientation: t=0 faces front, moving CCW toward +X as left side, back at t=0.5, right at 0.75. I'll place skulls around t=0.1-0.9 and bones/feathers at other positions, leaving a gap near the front for a flap. Building a skull helper with a sphere, jaw box, and dark eye sockets...

Adding bone-stick and feather helpers, then placing a large pendant skull along the draped necklace path at its midpoint, offset slightly downward and outward from the chest.

For attachment, I'm anchoring the skull to the upper spine joint rather than the tip, nudging it forward so it clears the body's surface. For the necklace itself, I'm distributing small beads along the path using bone-anchored spheres, considering alternating spikes between them but leaning toward skipping that detail for simplicity.

Adding alternating bone-and-gold colored beads with small downward-pointing claw spikes hanging off each one, using an explicit direction vector so they inherit the bead's bone and color. I'm skipping chin hair and a fur belt, then moving to the totem base — lathing a muddy rounded profile for the ground platform and defaulting all base props to anchor at the hips joint.

I'm applying a mottled mud texture with mossy patches based on surface normals, then placing a shallow teal water pool slightly ahead and between the troll's hands as a flat glowing disc, topped with lily pad cards for extra detail.

For the totem pole behind-left, I'm building a wooden post with carved grain texture, a glowing-eyed skull on top, tied feathers and bone cross-arms, and a face carved into the front using a plane layered just off the box surface rather than wrapping the texture around all six sides.

I'm giving the totem a slight tilt facing toward the troll, and colouring the face texture as a tribal carving in tan and red with the eyes glowing faintly green using a moderate glow strength. For the base, I'm scattering reed card clumps in a ring around the totem's base by computing frames at angled positions and placing leaning reed-textured cards there.

Reed heights should run roughly 0.6 to 1.1 and I'm keeping them clear of the troll by restricting placement to radius ≥1.0 along the back and sides, leaving the front pool area open. For extra detail, I'm adding four glowing purple mushrooms near the feet using lathe caps with white spots and a soft glow, then considering small floating firefly glow-spheres while skipping the stump seat idea.

Troll proportions settle around 2.3 units tall at the head with the mohawk peaking near 2.5, hunched posture included. I'm planning roughly six textures total: eye and facepaint SVGs, a totem face, reed texture, a gold rune pendant disc worn as a chest plaque, and tribal tattoo decals with scar lines layered into the skin paint for extra war-worn detail.

Now I'm setting up the module imports from the builder SDK, pulling in helpers for frames, randomness, curves, limbs, textures, and glow effects before writing the actual construction code.

Setting up skin material...

Warts use small stick spheres too. Now I'm setting up the build function: creating the builder, seeding the rng, and placing the hips joint as the root with a spine role, then building the spine chain upward through a catmull curve from hips to upper torso.

I'm sweeping the body along the spine chain skinned by bone, then adding a pelvis sphere and chest hump at the spine tip, followed by starting a neck chain from the spine's top joint.

Still writing limb code...

Still defining leg geometry... I'm positioning the foot box and toe capsules at ground level, with the ankle joint tying into the leg tip and claws added as small spikes on each toe.

Now I'm working out the arm chain from shoulder to wrist, setting the hand target position and sweep radii for the limb segments, then building the fist as a small box offset below the wrist joint.

Adding finger joints...

Adding lower teeth pointing upward, then placing eye and face paint decals onto the skull bone. I'm defining the mohawk as a surface spanning the body, neck, and skull sweeps, setting up height values along its profile.

Working out blade geometry...

I should fall back to the head bone if hit.bone is null. I'm also sketching two extra feather shapes behind the ear using leaf outlines in teal and orange, angled back and up near the mohawk.

Now I'm shifting to the loincloth, planning front and back flaps with a tribal zigzag pattern painted onto the cloth texture, defining coordinates relative to the attachment origin.

Positioning the front flap near the pelvis, checking clearance against the pelvis sphere radius so it doesn't intersect, and placing the back flap with opposite orientation so its thickness extends outward in the negative z direction.

For the belt, I'm computing a loop surface around the body-pelvis union, then deciding to use a skull as the buckle instead of a gold plate since a flat disc would overlap the flap geometry awkwardly—placing it slightly forward and larger to sit cleanly on top.

Now I'm positioning hanging trinkets along the belt loop at various parameter positions—small skulls, bone sticks, a bone cross, feather bundle, and a leather pouch—each offset outward along the belt's normal and dropped down via short cords, while checking that leg geometry under the hips doesn't clash with these hanging pieces.

I'm also writing a reusable skull helper that builds a cranium from a scaled sphere and a jaw from a box, parameterized by position, radius, and bone material so I can place multiple skull trinkets consistently.

Still writing skull/eye details...

For the totem, I'm starting a wooden pole using a rod sweep between two points with a tapered radius and grain texture.

Setting base radius to 1.3 and checking that the pool's position keeps safe distance from the troll's foot and hand placements. I'm adding a small water pool with a glowing teal cylinder, lily pads, and pink flower cones, then starting the lathe outline for the base geometry.

Working out the lathe points so the base profile stays non-self-intersecting, with ground level around 0.085. Now I'm setting up the mud texture using mottled color patches with moss accents for a natural, weathered look.

Adding scattered rocks around the base with dodecahedron shapes and flat moss shading, then placing a few mushrooms near the totem with lathe-shaped glowing caps and spotted stems. I'm also scattering small glowing octahedron wisps in green tones around the upper area, and generating reed card sprites arranged in a loop while leaving a clear arc open at the front.

Still working out texture setup...

The thick brow gives an angry look, so I'll remove the mirrored symmetry since it's unnecessary. Now I'm sketching the facepaint decal with diagonal white cheek stripes and red dots, then moving to a chest tattoo using teal and purple tribal spiral and sun motifs with simple thick strokes, and starting a totem face design next.

For the rune pendant, I'm deciding to repurpose the gold plaque disc with dark rune etching as a belt buckle instead of a necklace, placing it low on the belt near the skull decoration, with a possible second small skull accent -- skipping any glow effect for now.

I'm making the rune glow bright green against the dark disc for a magical effect, then thinking about adding gold rings around the tusk/pendant. Estimating around 200 total parts is fine, so now I'm focused on writing the actual code carefully, setting up helper functions for placing body parts with bone attachments and box geometry shortcuts.

Adding sphere helper and flat shading...

I'm defining the body's spine sweep with a radius function that tapers and bulges along the torso, wrapping it into a surface with the pelvis and other parts nested in. For the chest tattoo decal, I'm positioning it near the top of the torso while being mindful it might overlap with the necklace skull.

Deciding to move the tattoo to the belly instead to avoid clashing with the necklace, computing the surface point and normal direction there for the decal projection. For the necklace itself, I'm draping a cord path through catmull-rom control points and sweeping a thin tube along it in the cord color.

For the skull pendant, I'm placing it at the midpoint of the necklace path with a slight offset so it hangs naturally, and setting up a beads loop that alternates gold and bone-colored spheres along the drape, inheriting the bone frame from each path point.

For spikes hanging off beads, I'm attaching small downward cones at each bead frame. For belt items, I'm figuring out that querying the belt path at a parameter returns a raw position rather than a bone-aware frame, so those attachments will need to snap to the nearest hip joint instead.

For similar accessory paths like the necklace, chain, and tusks, I'm defining sweeps with tapered radii and flat-to-point end caps, and positioning the tusk base so it's embedded inside the jaw geometry rather than floating outside it.

Now I'm working out the ear extrusion, setting its outline direction along the outward x-axis with a thin thickness and attaching it to the head bone, then placing a gold hoop torus at the earlobe position with its axis oriented so the hole faces outward correctly.

I'm also sizing a hump sphere attached to the spine3 bone, checking that its top aligns properly with the mohawk and neck transitions, plus positioning a brow at the head bone. Now I'm setting up vector math for finger placement, building coordinate arrays for each joint.

Still writing totem pole geometry...

Adding feather details...

Now I'm placing scattered moss-covered rocks near the ground and finalizing joint names for the wrist chain. I'll write the full code now, using loose typing where necessary to keep things simple.
